title: Multi-Scale Markov-Switching GARCH Volatility Regime Gate for H026 ETF Portfolio
source: arXiv:2606.06190 (Chaudhary, Jun 2026) — "Multi-Scale Markov Switching GARCH: Volatility Regime Detection in EUR/USD"
summary: Chaudhary's triple-timeframe MS-GARCH framework operates simultaneously across Daily (macro), Weekly (meso), and Monthly (micro) scales, each using AR(1)-MS-GARCH with three hidden Calm/Turbulent/Crisis states. The outer-product of per-scale regime probabilities forms a 27-state cross-scale tensor; the paper proves this approach significantly outperforms single-timescale GARCH on volatility forecasting (Diebold-Mariano DM=+4.70, p=1.28e-6). H458 adapts this for the H026 25-ETF universe: fit a simplified two-scale (daily + weekly) MS-GARCH on the H026 equal-weight portfolio return, derive a composite Crisis probability, and use it as a position-sizing gate: full top-1 in Calm, top-2 in Turbulent, BIL in Crisis. Tractable implementation uses hmmlearn for each scale with GARCH-like variance features as emissions.
variants: Var A: Two-scale (daily+weekly) MS-GARCH gate — BIL when Crisis prob > 0.5, top-1 otherwise
Var B: Single-scale daily MS-GARCH — Calm/Turbulent/Crisis 3-state gate (comparison to H445)
Var C: Two-scale composite — top-2 in Turbulent, top-1 in Calm, BIL in Crisis
Var D: Crisis probability as continuous weight — scale position by (1 - crisis_prob), min weight 0
Var E: H026 H346 baseline (OB-gated top-2) — sanity check
gate: OOS Sharpe >= 3.238 (H346 canonical) AND MaxDD improvement vs -5.7% baseline
